newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU unlikely to agree on beef labels on Monday.
newsitem.headline: EU unlikely to agree on beef labels on Monday.

text.p: European Union farm ministers will make further progress on Monday on proposals to identify and register cattle and to label beef but are unlikely to reach agreement, EU diplomats said.

Various technical problems still have to be resolved and the European Parliament has not yet given an opinion on the proposed measures, which are intended to restore consumer confidence in beef after the mad cow disease health scare, they said.

In addition, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler's departure for Strasbourg on Tuesday morning means that there will not be enough time for the Dutch EU Presidency to prepare a compromise text and the meeting is likely to end on Monday.
Fischler is attending the weekly Commission meeting and a European Parliament debate on a report on the mad cow crisis.

On cattle registration and identification, diplomats said there were problems concerning financing, ear-tagging and deadlines for transmitting data. Some countries also say that the planned start-up in January, 1998, is unrealistic.
On beef labelling, six member states, including Germany and France, oppose the Commission's proposal for a voluntary system.
Diplomats said a possible compromise would be to review the situation in two years time with a commitment to move towards a compulsory system.
There is also disagrement over whether the label should include the country or region of birth as well as information on fattening and slaughtering.
